comments.body: Pushed as Gerrit 2062 (commit 9a0a16ef20), stacked on 2057. Held-out TDD: 9 tests authored, implementer saw only 3; the other 6 are divergence detectors. NOTE ON SHAPE: 8 of 9 passed before any implementation, because this consolidation has no new behaviour - so the held-out set is not 'edge cases the implementer could not see' but 'tests that catch an ERASED divergence'. The only genuinely RED requirement was the set-identity criterion. Both mutations killed by their exact held-out test: erasing the fc20 non-bug ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES narrowing killed test_the_non_bug_administrative_narrowing_is_preserved; flipping _recorded_replacement_target's on_subject_unreadable from 'continue' to 'stop' killed test_recorded_mode_continues_to_inbound_after_a_subject_reduce_failure. My FIRST attempt at that second mutation silently edited a DOCSTRING occurrence of the same literal and survived - worth recording, because a mutation that does not actually mutate reads exactly like a tautological test. Gates: lint rc=0, mypy 626 files clean, complexity new=0 increased=0 with two entries going stale (simpler), 72 pinning tests green with zero assertion edits, net -1 src lines, close_precheck.py 770 -> 726.

comments.body:
AC VERIFICATION against merged main (952ad4a0a6), run from a worktree at origin/main. Four of five criteria verified and ticked; ONE FAILS and the ticket therefore stays in_progress rather than being force-closed.

AC2 PASS (ticked). Pinning suites pass with no assertion edits. 'git show --numstat 952ad4a0a6 -- tests/' is a single line: '234 0 tests/unit/commands/test_replacement_walker.py' - additions only, one NEW file, zero deletions, and the four named pinning suites are untouched by that commit and by every commit since ('git log 952ad4a0a6..HEAD -- <the four files>' is empty). Ran them: 127 passed in 330s (test_close_disposition_attestation_738a.py, test_close_gate_disposition_69b9.py, test_close_precheck_duplicate_link_c8fd.py, tests/unit/commands/test_close_disposition.py, tests/unit/commands/test_replacement_walker.py, tests/unit/test_administrative_close_dispositions.py).

AC3 PASS (ticked). close_precheck.py:32 is now '_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES = close_disposition.DISPOSITION_CLASSES' - a plain alias, so the two ARE one object and cannot drift. test_the_disposition_class_sets_cannot_drift asserts 'is', not '==', exactly as the criterion demands. Passed.

AC4 PASS (ticked). The fc20 non-bug narrowing survives in the _has_live_replacement_link wrapper. test_the_non_bug_administrative_narrowing_is_preserved asserts 'not_a_bug' not in ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES, then that _has_live_replacement_link(bug_id, 'story', 'not_a_bug', tracker) is False while the same call with ticket_type='bug' is True against an identical live duplicates link - i.e. the exemption is still refused for a non-bug. Passed.

AC5 PASS (ticked), with the check mechanism noted. The substance is verified independently of the test: diffing 952ad4a0a6^ against HEAD, all three seams keep byte-identical signatures - _has_live_replacement_link(ticket_id, ticket_type, close_class, tracker) -> bool, _recorded_replacement_target(ticket_id, tracker) -> str | None, find_replacement(ticket_id, close_class, tracker) -> str | None. The landed test (test_the_three_seams_keep_their_names_and_signatures) checks this with 'assert hasattr(mod, name)' plus an inspect.signature arity assertion on find_replacement, rather than a literal monkeypatch.setattr(..., raising=True) as the AC's wording says. That is the logically equivalent condition - raising=True fails precisely when the attribute is absent - and the arity assertion is strictly stronger, so the criterion is met in substance; recorded here because the wording and the mechanism differ.

AC1 FAILS - LEFT UNTICKED. The uniqueness PROPERTY holds right now: only close_disposition.py contains both 'find_inbound_relationships(' and the '"supersedes"' literal under src/rebar; close_precheck.py has no find_inbound_relationships call left and exactly one 'supersedes' occurrence (:142, the user-facing remedy string, which was always meant to survive); and the reasoned escape marker exists at close_disposition.py:77 ('# replacement-walk-ok: this function is the SINGLE owner of the duplicates/supersedes walk'). But the criterion's stated oracle - 'checked by the guard test' - does not exist. 952ad4a0a6 added exactly one test file, tests/unit/commands/test_replacement_walker.py, and none of its 9 tests reads a source file: it contains no rglob, no read_text, no scan of src/rebar. Nor is there a scripts/check_*.py equivalent. So nothing fails when a second copy of the walk reappears.

This is not a wording nit. The construct-uniqueness guard is the whole thesis of the parent epic airborne-wellloved-kingfisher, whose guard-construction rule spells out the required shape (scan every file under src/rebar EXCEPT the owner module; match the conjunction of constituent atoms; provide the '# <construct>-ok: <why>' escape) and whose own first acceptance criterion reads 'checked by that child's construct-uniqueness test passing in the default Verified tier'. The epic cites tests/unit/test_spawn_detached.py::test_the_detached_spawn_signature_appears_only_in_proc as the model, and notes it caught a re-introduced copy (7213e082b5) two days after landing. Without that test this story delivers the consolidation but not the durability the epic exists to buy, and the epic's AC1 cannot be satisfied for this child.

REMEDIATION: land a construct-uniqueness guard modelled on test_the_detached_spawn_signature_appears_only_in_proc - scan src/rebar/**/*.py excluding close_disposition.py, flag any file containing 'find_inbound_relationships(' together with '"supersedes"', and honour a '# replacement-walk-ok: <why>' line marker. Then tick AC1 and close. Sibling note for the epic: the same gap exists on story vinyl-cheesy-termite (4329) - its test_lifecycle_cascade.py pins the _CASCADING_EDGES table's CONTENT but likewise does not scan src for a second walk; there the AC also named a grep, which does pass.

One separate observation, not an AC: close_precheck.py is 728 lines at HEAD, not the 726 recorded in the implementation comment - two lines came from a later commit. Still well under the 800 cap.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Three near-identical walkers discover a ticket's replacement link (iterate `deps` for `duplicates`, then `find_inbound_relationships` for `supersedes`): `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:58-108` (`_has_live_replacement_link`), `close_precheck.py:111-151` (`_recorded_replacement_target`), `src/rebar/_commands/close_disposition.py:76-118` (`find_replacement`), wrapped again by `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:166`. They differ only in liveness check and return type. Bug `frolicky-dependable-peccary` came from `verdict()` consulting only `find_replacement` while the "not_a_bug needs no link" rule lived in a comment in `_ensure_duplicate_close_is_linked` (`close_precheck.py:169-174`); the `DISPOSITION_CLASSES == _NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` equality is held only by a test (`close_disposition.py:43`).

## Approach
One `close_disposition.replacement_of(ticket_id, tracker, *, require_live: bool) -> str | None`; `_has_live_replacement_link` and `_recorded_replacement_target` become one-line wrappers kept as monkeypatch seams (the 738a tests patch the boolean). `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` imports `DISPOSITION_CLASSES` so the equality is structural. Guard: the `duplicates`/`supersedes` walk (`find_inbound_relationships(` combined with `"supersedes"`) appears only in `close_disposition.py`.


## Guard construction
Follow the guard-test construction rule in the parent epic `airborne-wellloved-kingfisher`: owner module exempt, match the constituent conjunction or AST shape named in Approach (or the definition count where no distinctive atom exists), `# <construct>-ok: <reason>` escape marker, and behaviour pinned only by the named existing tests.

## Scope
`src/rebar/_commands/close_disposition.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py`, `tests/unit/commands/test_close_disposition.py`.

## Testing
Happy path: a duplicate with a live target closes; edge: a duplicate whose target is itself closed-as-duplicate is refused; not_a_bug needs no link. Pinning: `tests/unit/test_close_disposition_attestation_738a.py`, `tests/unit/test_close_gate_disposition_69b9.py`, `tests/unit/test_close_precheck_duplicate_link_c8fd.py`, `tests/unit/commands/test_close_disposition.py` pass unchanged.


## The three walkers are NOT interchangeable — what the shared core may and may not absorb
Read of all three bodies before implementation (recorded so the collapse cannot silently change
behaviour):
- `find_replacement` (close_disposition.py:76) guards on `DISPOSITION_CLASSES` only and takes
  **no `ticket_type`**.
- `_has_live_replacement_link` (close_precheck.py:58) guards on `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES`
  **and additionally narrows non-bug tickets to `ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES`** (ticket fc20). It is
  therefore STRICTLY LESS permissive than `find_replacement` for non-bug tickets.
- `_recorded_replacement_target` (close_precheck.py:111) has **no class guard at all**, and on a
  failed `reduce_ticket` it **continues to the inbound pass** where the other two return early.
  Its caller pre-filters to `{duplicate, superseded}`.

Therefore the shared core is the **walk plus the liveness mode only** —
`replacement_of(ticket_id, tracker, *, require_live)` performs the `duplicates` outbound scan
then the `supersedes` inbound scan, applying `_is_live_ticket` iff `require_live`. **Class and
ticket_type filtering stays at each wrapper**, because the three differ there and merging them
would change which closes are exempt. The reduce-failure divergence is preserved EXPLICITLY, not by
argument. An earlier revision claimed the two live-mode callers were "unaffected because a failed
reduce yields no outbound candidate either way" — that reasoning covers only the OUTBOUND scan.
`find_replacement` returns `None` on a subject reduce failure BEFORE reaching the inbound pass
(`close_disposition.py:92-97`), so a core that always continued to inbound could return a live
`supersedes` source where today it fails closed. That would weaken a fail-closed verification
path. The core therefore takes the reduce-failure posture as a parameter:
`on_subject_unreadable="stop"` for the two live-mode callers (matching today's early return) and
`"continue"` for `_recorded_replacement_target`, whose whole job is the strictly weaker "was one
ever recorded?" question and which deliberately continues today.

## Rename hazard: the monkeypatch seams must keep their names
`_has_live_replacement_link` is patched with **`raising=False`** at
`tests/unit/test_close_disposition_attestation_738a.py:94` and `:130`. With `raising=False` a
RENAME does not fail at patch time — it silently installs an unused attribute, and
`test_a_force_close_is_still_never_signed_even_for_a_linked_duplicate` would still go GREEN
while no longer testing what it claims. `_has_live_replacement_link` and
`_recorded_replacement_target` therefore stay as named one-line wrappers, and
`find_replacement` keeps its 3-positional-arg signature (patched at 738a:48 and
`tests/unit/commands/test_close_disposition.py:138,161`; called positionally at 738a:174).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The replacement-link **walk** has one body: the construct `find_inbound_relationships(` in conjunction with `"supersedes"` appears under `src/rebar` only in `close_disposition.py`, with a reasoned `# replacement-walk-ok: <why>` escape; checked by the guard test.
- [x] Pinning suites pass with no assertion edits; checked by `pytest` and `git diff --stat`.
- [x] `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` (defined at `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:28`) is derived from `close_disposition.DISPOSITION_CLASSES` (defined at `close_disposition.py:44`) rather than restated, so the two cannot drift; checked by a test asserting the two sets are the SAME object, not merely equal.

## Review remediation (2026-08-21)
Three blocking findings on the previous ACs, all verified against the tree:
1. **The old AC1 was unachievable.** It demanded `grep -c "supersedes" src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py` equal to `0`, but `supersedes` legitimately occurs there four times: `:67` (a docstring explaining the disposition), `:105` and `:146` (the walk itself, which does move), and `:186` (the user-facing remedy string `rebar link <replacement> {ticket_id} supersedes`). Only the WALK is consolidated; the docstring and the remedy string must survive, so a whole-token grep is the wrong oracle. AC1 now names the walk's constituent conjunction, per the parent epic's guard rule #2.
2. **The old AC3 named the wrong file.** It said `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` is "checked by reading `txn.py`"; that constant is defined at `close_precheck.py:28` and does not appear in `txn.py`. AC3 now names both real locations.
3. **"Checked by reading" is not a check.** AC3 now requires an identity assertion (same object), which is what actually prevents the two sets drifting apart — the drift that bug `frolicky-dependable-peccary` came from.
- [x] The non-bug ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES narrowing that only `_has_live_replacement_link` applies is preserved; checked by a test closing a non-bug ticket as `not_a_bug` and asserting the exemption is still refused.
- [x] `_has_live_replacement_link`, `_recorded_replacement_target` and `find_replacement` keep their exact names and signatures as monkeypatch seams; checked by a test that patches each by name with `raising=True`.
